courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

lectures.title: Managing the User with a Subject

cues.en: Now that we added sign-up and sign in,
it's important to also manage the login state in our application correctly.
Now we'll need a couple things, for example we'll need that token and therefore here, I will actually
add a new private property token which is null initially where I want to store that token. Now in get
userIsAuthenticated,
I actually now don't want to use my private userIsAuthenticated variable anymore,
instead I'll remove that
but here the existence of a token, of a valid token will actually determine whether we should be logged
in or not.
So for now what I can return here is simply the answer to the question whether we have a token or
not.
However the token should not be managed like this but instead in a behavior subject, so that whenever it changes,
we can tell this to the entire application
and for example log us out and automatically redirect us, which I would want to do.
So let's create a new behavior subject here which actually will yield a string because the token is
a string and behavior subject needs to be imported from rxjs
and let's do the same for the userId and therefore, we could actually merge both into one user object.
So let's add a new user model here where we can export a class, user and in there, I'll add a constructor
and that constructor will set a public property ID which is a string, so that userId, we also can
store an e-mail in here
so that would also be a string and
I also want to store the token but in a private property, that will be a string
and I also want to store the token expiration date because that will be important,
token is not valid forever, it will expire and that will be a date. Now
next to all these fields, I'll also add a getter for a token property,
so this one is named _token,
this one is the one we can publicly access and we can only get that and here
I basically want to check if we're not having an expiration date, in which case the token would be invalid
or if this token expiration date is smaller or equal than the current date, new date gives us a current
timestamp, not just the date but also the time.
In that case, I would return null here for the token, so then the token would be invalid, otherwise I will
return
this _token. And now with that user model added which manages its own basic token validation and
checks if it's still valid or is still up-to-date, with that, we can add a new private property in the auth
service, _user which now is the actual new behavior subject I want to use and therefore I'll
get rid of the token here as well and that will eventually yield us a user.
So that is the generic type
assigned here and of course I import user from the user model I just added and now it's this user I want
to manage in here.
Now we can still have our get userIsAuthenticated helper and there in the end, it depends and we need
to find out whether our current user has a valid token or not. Now I'll initialize the user here with
null by the way
and then here in get userIsAuthenticated,
I will return this user as observable, pipe because I want to not return the full user here but only the
information whether this user is authenticated or not
and therefore I'll pipe the map operator here to transform the data in the user subject which is a
user object,
I want to transform it to a boolean,
therefore this map operator is imported from rxjs operators and then down there in the map operator,
we get that full user object and I want to return the answer to the question whether that user is authenticated
or not,
well that simply depends on whether we have a valid token or not.
So I can return user token here,
however I will actually add two exclamation marks here which will convert this to a boolean because the
token by default is a string, if
I would add one exclamation mark, I would return true if the token is invalid and false if it is valid,
if I add two,
I basically just force a conversion to a boolean.
So this now returns an observable that will eventually yield true or false depending on whether we
have a token or not.
Now for the userId, if we need that, then I can just return
this user has observable and there I'll also map the response and I'll get my full user object here
but I actually only want to get the ID, so I can just access userId and return that. Now to avoid
errors
if user is undefined or is null as it is at the beginning here, I should of course also take
care about such scenarios and therefore I will actually wrap these checks here, so I'll not just use the short
inline notation but I will eventually return this but only if we have a user object, so I'll check if user
is set
in which case I then return this token which I tried to access,
otherwise if we have no user, then I just return false
because then the user certainly is not authenticated
if we have no user and I'll do the same here for the userId,
I will actually not use the short notation where I have everything inlined. I do return my userId
here but only if we have a user,
so if user, then I try to return the userId, else I will just return null here.
So now we adjusted these two getters and we are now using the user model to also manage our state.
Therefore here in logout, what I of course want to do is I want to reach out to my user subject and
emit a new event where I reset the user to null
but of course I'll also have to make sure that I do actually set a user
after we logged in or signed up and that will be the next step.
